input.summary:
Front part (fenestration and front) now builds with 0 refused writes and 0 off-palette blocks: the six cut_sandstone lintels at y=16 that the locked shell had already laid in brick are no longer written (windowNoSill now writes panes only).
make.sh runs clean and wrote build.nbt; the front part places 374 blocks.
The palette check was already clean before the fix, so only the refusals changed.

waste.what: Finding which cells the locked shell had already filled: I read the built grid cell by cell with a one-off node script to see that y=16 at x=4..6 and 24..26 was brick, not air.
waste.cost: 1 node probe over 12 cells, plus a second make run to confirm
waste.tool: `mcd plan`/`mcd check --contract` should list each part's writes that would hit an earlier part's cells, with the existing block, before make.sh runs

waste.what: The silent skip in windowDress: its put() drops non-air writes into skipped counts, and note() in front.mjs tests `res.skipped.length` on a number, so it never prints. Dozens of head writes (A 2-wide lintel at x7..10 y16; every B quartz head at y6, 9, 14, 19) vanish with no report.
waste.cost: about 1 minute of reading to find, since the make output showed no warning at all
waste.tool: the build library's runParts report should count skipped helper writes per part, not only guard refusals; or the helper's `skipped` should be a number checked with `> 0`

left: A's second-floor windows at x=4..6 and C's at x=24..26 now take the shell's brick lintel instead of the planned cut_sandstone head (the shell is locked, so this is the only fix available here). Restoring the stone lintel means changing the shell's brick course at y=16.

windowDress silently skips every head that the shell already built, and note() never reports it, because it tests `.length` on a number. Skipped heads: the A 2-wide window's lintel at x=7..10 y=16, and all the B quartz heads (smooth_quartz at y=6, 9, 14, 19 across x=12..18). Those heads are missing from the build. Fixing note() to report `skipped > 0` would expose them; I left it alone because the brief was to fix only the reported refusals.

The A and C second-floor window sills (smooth_sandstone_slab at y=12, z=11) sit in the bay room cells (x=8..9, z=11), so they overlap the bay deck level the roofs part owns. Not checked against the roofs part.
